2026-03-07T17:48:03.6348089Z ## Report Structure Guidelines
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6348271Z 
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6348368Z ### 1. Header Levels
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6348779Z **Use h3 (###) or lower for all headers in your issue report to maintain proper document hierarchy.**
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6349159Z 
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6349284Z When creating GitHub issues or discussions:
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6349642Z - Use `###` (h3) for main sections (e.g., "### Test Summary")
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6350052Z - Use `####` (h4) for subsections (e.g., "#### Device-Specific Results")
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6350507Z - Never use `##` (h2) or `#` (h1) in reports - these are reserved for titles
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6350791Z 
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6350906Z ### 2. Progressive Disclosure
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6351475Z **Wrap detailed test results in `<details><summary><b>Section Name</b></summary>` tags to improve readability and reduce scrolling.**
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6351979Z 
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6352087Z Use collapsible sections for:
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6352385Z - Verbose details (full test logs, raw data)
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6352759Z - Secondary information (minor warnings, extra context)
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6353143Z - Per-item breakdowns when there are many items
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6353367Z 
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6353610Z Always keep critical information visible (summary, critical issues, key metrics).
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6353953Z 
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6354061Z ### 3. Report Structure Pattern
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6354241Z 
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6354402Z 1. **Overview**: 1-2 paragraphs summarizing key findings
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6354852Z 2. **Critical Information**: Show immediately (summary stats, critical issues)
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6355402Z 3. **Details**: Use `<details><summary><b>Section Name</b></summary>` for expanded content
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6356086Z 4. **Context**: Add helpful metadata (workflow run, date, trigger)
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6356406Z 
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6356531Z ### Design Principles (Airbnb-Inspired)
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6356743Z 
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6356834Z Reports should:
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6357339Z - **Build trust through clarity**: Most important info immediately visible

2026-03-07T17:48:03.6409276Z ### 2.2 Simplification Principles
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6409459Z 
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6409618Z Apply these refinements to the recently modified code:
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6410031Z 
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6410145Z #### 1. Preserve Functionality
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6410476Z - **NEVER** change what the code does - only how it does it
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6410909Z - All original features, outputs, and behaviors must remain intact
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6411343Z - Run tests before and after to ensure no behavioral changes
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6411609Z 
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6411705Z #### 2. Enhance Clarity
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6411981Z - Reduce unnecessary complexity and nesting
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6412310Z - Eliminate redundant code and abstractions
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6412696Z - Improve readability through clear variable and function names
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6413075Z - Consolidate related logic
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6413391Z - Remove unnecessary comments that describe obvious code
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6413894Z - **IMPORTANT**: Avoid nested ternary operators - prefer switch statements or if/else chains
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6414477Z - Choose clarity over brevity - explicit code is often better than compact code
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6414811Z 
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6414915Z #### 3. Apply Project Standards
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6415212Z - Use project-specific conventions and patterns
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6415545Z - Follow established naming conventions
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6415842Z - Apply consistent formatting
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6416459Z - Use appropriate language features (modern syntax where beneficial)
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6416923Z 
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6417020Z #### 4. Maintain Balance
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6417286Z Avoid over-simplification that could:
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6417592Z - Reduce code clarity or maintainability
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6417960Z - Create overly clever solutions that are hard to understand
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6418387Z - Combine too many concerns into single functions or components
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6418820Z - Remove helpful abstractions that improve code organization
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6419327Z - Prioritize "fewer lines" over readability (e.g., nested ternaries, dense one-liners)
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6419786Z - Make the code harder to debug or extend
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6419993Z 
2026-03-07T17:48:03.6420093Z ### 2.3 Perform Code Analysis

2026-03-07T17:48:03.6424024Z    - What patterns should be applied?
